patient.chief_complaint: Campus police and EMS called after student found convulsing in dormitory hallway, 12 minutes duration
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. White is a 24-year-old college student with no prior epilepsy who is brought by campus EMS after being found convulsing in his dormitory hallway by a friend. The friend reports that the patient attended an off-campus party last night where he used MDMA (3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine, ecstasy) approximately 8 hours prior to seizure onset. He appears to have developed a seizure while returning to his room. The friend estimated continuous seizure activity for approximately 12 minutes before EMS arrived. No prior seizures. He is on buspirone for anxiety. His temperature on arrival is 40.2°C.

output.summary: Rhabdomyolysis with AKI: CK above 10,000 U/L is associated with high risk for acute kidney injury. Aggressive IV isotonic saline targeting urine output 1–3 mL/kg/h is standard management. Hyperthermia is a potent driver of ongoing muscle breakdown; temperature management is integral to limiting CK rise. Hyperkalaemia from rhabdomyolysis requires cardiac monitoring; calcium gluconate and renal replacement therapy may be required in severe cases.

useless_tools.rationale: No clinical suspicion of cardiac source of embolus or cardiogenic seizure; routine echo is not indicated in SE workup absent cardiac findings.
